findings.interpretation: Service/backlog stall, not offer-dispatch delay. Maintenance overlaps all candidate tail cohorts, but most trial2/3 slow requests start outside recorded maintenance windows. Long requests naturally span more periodic waves, so overlap is not exclusive causal attribution.

Dispatch improves while service tails worsen. Scheduled checkpoint/reclaim intervals cannot be the sole explanation; background follower catchup may continue after those intervals and is not timestamped.
Counts do not increase consistently with regressions; only replica3 aggregate, no per-install timing or bytes. Neither rule out nor establish snapshot/catchup cause.

facts: Fixture observes checkpoint completion then enqueues reclamation for all3replicas in the same reactor turn; later waves require that active reclamation set complete.

NativeLogWorker processes Work::Reclaim synchronously on its single store-owning worker before receiving another queued work item. This is a possible durable-service delay path, not proof it caused a particular recorded gap.
NativeLogStore::reclaim encodes/decodes/verifies full checkpoint state and only replaces the log when shorter; no comparison/durability shortcut or speculative publication is warranted.

recommendation: Smallest next step is a source ordering audit of existing foreground persistence, queued reclamation and snapshot send/install completion paths: establish what can keep an original waiting after scheduled maintenance rows end, and how a cold group shares those owners/budgets. Use existing deterministic held-completion fixtures to reason about exact ordering if needed. Do not change checkpoint frequency or fixture scheduling to hide cost, revive rejected fusion/pipeline, or add a new measurement/observer prerequisite. Existing data identifies service-side stalls but lacks per-original commit/physical-barrier/install timestamps, so it does not justify a specific allocator/network-loss/filesystem fix. Keep480 a measured tradeoff with guard regressions open; fullP9 remains active.
limits: No new benchmark, profile, observer, remote operation or production edit. Correlation is separated from unidentifiable causes; cumulative/nested wall counters are not additive CPU time.
